newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE'S MAS SAYS NO PLANS FOR PRESS CONFERENCE.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE'S MAS SAYS NO PLANS FOR PRESS CONFERENCE.

text.p: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said on Friday morning it has no plans to hold a press conference today.
"We have heard of the rumours that MAS is planning a press conference this morning at 11 am. But as far as I am aware, there is no press conference being arranged," a MAS spokesman told Reuters.
He added that there was no press conference planned for today.
Dealers said rumours have been circulating that the MAS, the country's de facto central bank, would be holding a briefing on the issue of foreign shareholding limits of banks.
Under current Singapore laws, foreigners can only hold up to 40 percent of bank shares.
Shares of Singapore's four major banks, namely DBS Bank, OCBC Bank, United Overseas Bank and Overseas Union Bank have separate quotations for their local and foreign tranches.

The bank shares saw volatile trading on the last few days on speculation that changes may be made to the foreign shareholding limits. Local bank shares have soared to new year highs while foreign shares have plunged.
